newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Dominion has 50 percent E.Midland acceptances.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dominion has 50 percent E.Midland acceptances.

text.p: Dominion Resources, the U.S. energy group, said on Thursday it had acceptances representing 50.3 percent of shares in UK regional electricity company (Rec) East Midlands Electricity as part of its plan to takeover the running of the British utility.
Dominion, which has made a $2.15 billion agreed bid for East Midlands, said it had on Thursday purchased some 15 percent of East Midland's ordinary share capital at 670 pence per share.

The UK government on Wednesday said it would not be referring the bid to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang said that Dominion had given assurances to address regulatory concerns.

Dominion said that as of 1500 GMT on Thursday it had received acceptances representing approximately 35.3 percent of the ordinary capital of East Midlands. Its 670 pence per share offer is open until January 10.
It said that the 15 percent stake had been purchased on its behalf by DR Investments, a wholly owned subsidiary of Dominion.
East Midlands shares closed 3 1/2p firmer at 665p on Thursday.

U.S.-based firms have already snapped up a number of the original 12 cash-rich British regional electricity companies, with London Electricity the latest to fall. U.S. group Entergy on Wednesday agreed to pay $2.1 billion for control of London.
Meanwhile CE Electric has made a hostile bid for Northern Electric. Yorkshire and Southern Electricity remain the only two of the dozen Recs without suitors.
